questions.title: Blood lactic acid during and after a sprint
questions.stimulus: An athlete runs a 4-minute maximum-effort sprint on a treadmill and then rests for 14 minutes. The graph shows how the concentration of lactic acid in the athlete's blood changes over time.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the peak blood lactic acid concentration reached at the end of the sprint.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the blood lactic acid concentration rises steeply between 2 minutes and 6 minutes.

points.text: Muscles contract rapidly and need more energy / ATP
Heart and lungs cannot supply enough oxygen to the muscle cells fast enough
Aerobic respiration alone cannot meet the energy demand
Muscle cells carry out anaerobic respiration (incomplete breakdown of glucose)
Lactic acid builds up in the muscles and diffuses into the blood

accept: oxygen supply is insufficient for aerobic respiration
reject: there is no oxygen at all

parts.label: c
parts.text: Name the term used for the extra oxygen required during recovery (6 to 20 minutes) to break down the lactic acid.

questions.title: Heat released by germinating beans
questions.stimulus: A student investigates whether germinating beans release thermal energy during respiration. Equal masses of live germinating beans and boiled, cooled beans are placed into identical vacuum flasks for 48 hours.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Calculate the temperature difference between Flask A and Flask B after 48 hours.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the beans in both flasks were washed in disinfectant before the start of the investigation.

points.text: To kill microorganisms / bacteria / fungi on the surface of the beans
Their respiration does not release extra heat (so any temperature rise is caused only by the beans)

accept: prevents microbes respiring and warming the flask
reject: to clean them / make it hygienic

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain the purpose of using (i) vacuum flasks and (ii) Flask B containing boiled beans.

points.text: Vacuum flasks: insulate the contents / reduce heat loss to the surroundings
Flask B (boiled beans): acts as a control to show that living/respiring seeds cause the temperature rise (not the apparatus or room temperature)

accept: boiling denatures enzymes so dead seeds cannot respire
reject: to make it a fair test (unqualified)

questions.title: Aerobic respiration in cells
questions.stimulus: The diagram shows an animal cell with four subcellular structures labelled A, B, C and D.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name structure D, where most of the reactions of aerobic respiration take place.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write the balanced chemical symbol equation for aerobic respiration.

points.text: All four chemical formulae correct: C₆H₁₂O₆ + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O

accept: '+ energy' or '+ ATP' written on the right-hand side

parts.label: c
parts.text: Name the molecule produced by respiration that transfers energy for cellular processes such as active transport.
